speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe any other symptoms you are experiencing, such as abdominal pain, fever, or changes in your urine and stool color? Have you had any recent travel, new medications, or exposure to alcohol or illicit substances?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent jaundice and agitation, I need to rule out acute liver injury, so I will order blood work to check your liver enzymes, bilirubin, and viral hepatitis serologies. REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Hepatitis A, B, and C serologies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated); AST: 600 IU/L (elevated); ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated); TP Activity: < 40% (reduced); INR: 1.5 (elevated). Hepatitis A, B, and C serology results are not available in the provided data. NORMAL READINGS for requested viral serologies.

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative viral hepatitis serologies and significantly reduced prothrombin activity point toward acute liver failure, likely toxic in origin. Given your history of substance use, have you taken any acetaminophen or other over-the-counter pain relievers recently, and did you consume alcohol on the same days?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative viral serologies and significant liver dysfunction, I need to rule out acetaminophen toxicity, which is common with recreational drug use. speaker: Doctor
text: With viral, autoimmune, and common toxic causes ruled out, I suspect acute liver failure secondary to ecstasy or cocaine toxicity, possibly exacerbated by rhabdomyolysis. REQUEST TEST: Serum creatine kinase, Coagulation profile, Blood gas analysis

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of acute liver failure with coagulopathy, agitation, and a history of ecstasy use strongly suggests serotonin syndrome or direct hepatotoxicity from MDMA, especially given the exclusion of viral, autoimmune, and acetaminophen causes. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute liver failure secondary to MDMA (Ecstasy) toxicity
